label_sections.body: Found in the sun-bleached mudstones of Montana, this specimen was initially just a cluster of brown fragments. It took 200 hours of precision air-abrasion to reveal the bone beneath the rock.

Isotope analysis of the tooth enamel reveals this animal was a traveler. It spent its summers drinking snowmelt in the mountains before migrating 300 miles to the coastal deltas to avoid the winter chill.
The skull on display is a 3D-printed reconstruction. The original fossil was too fragile to mount, so we used Micro-CT scans to 'virtually' repair the crushing caused by 66 million years of burial.
